transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... I guess I'm here because of my face. I just... I can't really stop thinking about how the left side of it looks. It's... it's crooked. Just messed up. 

When I'm at work at the warehouse, or... or out at salsa night, I just know everyone is noticing it. Even though they always tell me they don't see anything. But... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking your face in the mirror, because of how you feel about your appearance?

Yeah... I guess. Like at work, before I go back out on the inventory floor... I end up in the bathroom a lot. Just checking the mirror. I try to fix my cap, or... I just keep rubbing at the same spot on my face. 

I don't mean to take so long, but... sometimes I'm late getting back out there. My picking numbers fall behind, and... my boss gets on me about it again. So... yeah. I do that.
Is it only your face that you're concerned about, or are there other parts of your body that you worry about as well?
Um... no. Just... just my face. I don't really... I mean, that's the only part that's messed up. So... yeah. Just that.
Do you feel like you have to perform these rituals, like rubbing your face or checking the mirror, or can you stop yourself if you want to?
I don't know. I just... I do it. I don't really think about stopping. It just happens.
Do you feel less anxious after you've checked your face in the mirror or rubbed the spot that bothers you?

Um... not really. I don't know. 

It doesn't... it doesn't really make it better. I just... I still feel the same after. So, no. I guess not.
Do you feel like the spot on your face that you rub needs to be perfect or symmetrical in some way?
I don't know. Not really. I don't really think about it like that. It's not about being... symmetrical or anything. It's just messed up. So... no.
Do you have thoughts about your face that keep repeating in your mind, even when you're trying to focus on something else?

Yeah... I guess so. I just... I can't really stop thinking about it. Like... how the left side of my face is just... crooked. And messed up. 

It's just always in my head. Like when I'm working at the warehouse, or... or even if I try to go to salsa night. I just keep thinking everyone is noticing it. They tell me they don't see anything, but... I don't know. I just can't stop thinking about it.
Do you try to ignore or push away these thoughts about your face being crooked?

I don't know. Um... not really, I guess. 

They're just... they're just always there. I don't really know how I would push them away. So... no.
Do you feel like the thoughts about your face being crooked are unwanted or are they something you intentionally think about?
I don't know. I don't really... try to think about it, I guess. It's just my face. So... I'm not sure.
Do you think your concerns about your face are unreasonable?
Um... no. I don't really... I don't think so. It's just... it's just what I look like. So... no.
Do you feel like something bad would happen if you didn't check your face in the mirror or rub the spot that bothers you?
Um... no. I don't think so. I don't really... think about it like that. I just... do it. So... no. Not really.
Do you feel like your face would be okay if it was just a little bit crooked, or does it need to look a certain way for you to feel okay about it?
Um... I don't really know. It just... shouldn't be crooked. I just want it to look right, I guess. So... yeah. I'm not really sure how to answer that.
Do you think your face would look okay if someone else thought it looked fine, even if you still see it as crooked?
Um... probably not. I mean... if I can still see it, then it's still there. It doesn't really matter what anyone else says about it. It's still wrong. So... no.
Do you think you would still feel the need to check your face in the mirror or rub the spot if you couldn't see yourself, like if you were blindfolded?
Um... I don't really know. I've never... been blindfolded or anything like that. So... I couldn't really tell you. I just don't know.
Do you think your behavior of checking and rubbing your face would stop if a doctor told you that there is actually nothing wrong with your face?
I don't think so. I mean, doctors have told me it's fine before, but... I can still feel it. So, I don't think it would change anything.
Do you think your face would look okay if it was perfectly symmetrical, but still had the features that you currently see as flaws?

Um... I'm not really sure. I can't really... picture what that would look like. If the things that are wrong are still there, then... I don't know. I guess not. I haven't really thought about it like that.
Do you think your face would be acceptable to you if the left and right sides were symmetrical, even if they still didn't look perfect?
I... I think that's kind of what you just asked me. I really don't know. If it still doesn't look right, then... probably not. I just can't see it being okay.
Do you think your face would look okay if the left and right sides were a little different, as long as you couldn't see any flaws?
I don't really... I don't know. If the things I see weren't there, then... maybe? But I just... I can't really picture it. It's hard to imagine it not looking wrong. I don't know.
Do you think your face would look okay if someone else fixed the part that you see as crooked, even if you couldn't see what they did?
I... I don't know. If I can't see it, how would I know if it's fixed? I just... I can't really answer that.
Do you think your face would look okay if it was completely normal-looking to others, but still felt wrong to you?
I don't think so. If it still feels wrong... I don't know how that would be okay. I just... it wouldn't be.
